cards.q: Why does Scaled Dot-Product Attention divide $QK^\top$ by $\sqrt{d_k}$ before applying softmax?
cards.a: If $q$ and $k$ have mean $0$ and variance $1$, their dot product has variance $d_k$. Dividing by $\sqrt{d_k}$ keeps variance at $1$ so softmax does not saturate into one-hot probabilities with near-zero gradients.

cards.q: In LoRA ($h = W_0 x + \frac{\alpha}{r} B A x$), how are $A$ and $B$ initialized at step 0, and why?
cards.a: $A$ is initialized with Gaussian noise and $B = 0$. That ensures $\Delta W = BA = 0$ at step $0$ (no change to the base model) while giving $B$ a nonzero gradient on the very first backward pass.
